title: Throughput playbook — daily todo & triage
content:
Daily scratchpad — throughput playbook (personal)
Owner: Noelle Ramos
Context: quick-running checklist and triage script for throughput regressions on dedicated pools. Keep lightweight; handoff-ready.

AM NOTES (2026-03-12):
- Observed 15% drop in avg throughput on gpu-pool-2 during 09:10–09:40 window. No error spikes, only increased queues.
- Alert: route=/generate, model=redwood-3b-8k-quant, p99 latency +50ms; throughput drop aligns with small surge of long-context requests (~1% of traffic) but may be batching related.

Immediate quick checks (run in order):
1) Check running queue/backlog: curl admin endpoint or `kubectl exec` into queue-agent.
   - cmd: kubectl exec -n inference svc/queue-read -- curl -sS http://localhost:8080/metrics | egrep 'request_queue_size'
2) Verify worker utilization and GPU SM util: nvidia-smi dmon && prometheus-panel gpu_utilization (last 15m)
3) KV cache hitrate: GET /cache/stats for model redwood-3b-8k-quant
   - if hitrate drops >10% vs baseline, hypothesis: kv-eviction thrash due to mixed short/long contexts
4) Check batching distribution: /debug/batching-histogram route on gateway for model.

Observed quick outputs:
- queue_size peaked at 230 -> normal steady-state ~120
- gpu_util: 72% avg, with short drops to 45% (scheduling gaps)
- kv_cache_hitrate: 81% (baseline 92%)
- batching histogram: 60% single-request batches, 25% small batches of 2–3, 15% >=8 (long requests skewing)

Hypotheses: 
A) Long-context requests break batching packing (prefixes don't align) causing many small batches -> throughput drop.
B) KV eviction policy currently LRU with fixed shard size; mixed seq lengths lead to higher miss rate -> more compute per token.
C) Scheduler protection/circuit-breaker tripping briefly on specific shard -> reduces available slots and increases queue.

Short experiments (what to run now):
- EXP-1: Enable microbatch-shim that groups single-request batches into fixed 4-frame windows for 60s on a canary host. Measures: qps, p50/p99, GPU util, kv_hitrate.
  - patch: runtime/patches/microbatch-shim-canary (apply to instance gpu-pool-2-azb)
- EXP-2: Temporarily increase KV shard memory for redwood-3b-8k-quant by +20% for 30m. Observe kv_hitrate and p99.
- EXP-3: Adjust circuit-breaker cooldown from 10s to 5s for route=/generate (canary).

Commands to run (copy-paste):
- kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/gateway-canary --field-manager=noelle-playbook
- curl -X POST "http://admin:7000/ops/patch?name=microbatch-shim&target=canary" -d '{\"window_ms\":50,\"max_group\":4}'
- prometheus query: rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count{route='/generate'}[5m])

Data to capture (attach to ticket INF-482):
- Prometheus panels: request_rate, queue_size, gpu_utilization, kv_cache_hitrate, batching_histogram (15m before/after)
- p50/p95/p99 for tokens/seq_length buckets (short <512, mid 512–2048, long >2048)
- logs: gateway debug + runtime worker logs (grep TRACE microbatch)

Notes to self (observational):
- When batching falls below avg 3, GPU SM utilization oscillates more — likely kernel launch inefficiency for many tiny batches. Worth testing launch pre-warm heuristic.
- NUMA pinning on recent node images might have subtle I/O impact for KV access; check dmesg for DMA warnings on nodes used during incident.

Longer-term playbook items (backlog):
- [ ] Add an automated canary run that simulates 1% long-context requests mixed with base traffic for cert pipelines. (ideal: nightly)
- [ ] Implement adaptive microbatch window: start 8ms, ramp to 64ms if batch rate low, cap by latency SLOs.
- [ ] Revisit KV eviction: consider segmented LRU per-seq-length or small hot-set pinning (TTL for prefix-heavy models).
- [ ] Kernel-level: experiment with CUDA stream pooling and persistent kernels for small batches (reduce launch overhead).
- [ ] Add metric: batching_efficiency = effective_tokens / theoretical_max_tokens per-second per-GPU.

Follow-ups and owners:
- Lina: run EXP-1 on canary and post prometheus exports to INF-482 (due today EOD)
- Ethan: apply KV memory bump and monitor (30m window)
- Rajiv: check node-level NUMA / dmesg for the two nodes in question and call out any warnings

Log snippets to keep:
- runtime worker trace (2026-03-12 09:12:17): \"small-batch path took 12ms (launch 7ms, kernel 3ms, overhead 2ms)\"
- gateway debug (2026-03-12 09:11:58): \"batcher: flush due to timeout, size=1, route=/generate\"

Quick TODO (today):
- [ ] Kick off EXP-1 canary (10m) -> Lina
- [ ] Bump KV shard memory on redwood-3b-8k-quant -> Ethan
- [ ] Collect and attach panels to INF-482 (Noelle)
- [ ] If canary shows improvement, plan rollout to 10% nodes then 50% (document rollback criteria)

Questions I'm still unsure about (to discuss at daily):
- Is there any autoscaler smoothing that might be dropping worker pods at the wrong time (check vertical/horizontal scaling events)?
- Should we consider rejecting >8k token requests at gateway with a soft 503 and suggest chunking? Pros/cons for user experience vs throughput.

Notes-to-self: keep this document minimal — move final playbook to Confluence only after 2 successful canaries.

End of day: capture final numbers and write short postmortem blurb to INF-482.
